# Offline-First Static Deliverable

The deliverable must work by **double-clicking a file**: no server, no install, no network. Seven
repositories build this way, and in two of them it is stated as a value rather than a convenience.

## Evidence

> "Farely runs **fully on-device**"
> — Farley/README.md, 2026-07-24

> "      // addAll is atomic; cache individually so one miss doesn't abort install"
> — Physics/exam_prep/sw.js, 2026-07-10

The second quote is the pattern taken seriously: an installable PWA whose service worker caches
per-URL because one missing file would otherwise abort the whole offline install. See
[[cache-individually-not-addall]].

## The instances

- `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` — `lab4_Complexity/part2` and `lab6_Neo4j/viewer/` contain zero
  external URLs; the lab-6 viewer reimplements every Cypher query in JS as "the exact analogue" so the
  graph can be explored without a database running. See [[dual-implementation-as-cross-check]].
- `Physics` — a full installable PWA: `manifest.webmanifest`, hand-written `sw.js`, KaTeX vendored
  locally with 20 font files so no CDN is needed. See [[vendor-katex-instead-of-cdn]].
- `labour-fraud-analysis` — a deliberate *second* entry point: `serve.py` is 60 lines of stdlib
  `http.server`, and `interactive/vendor/` commits all six third-party JS libraries so there is no npm.
- `privacy-policy` — one self-contained `index.html`, inline `<style>`, `prefers-color-scheme` light
  and dark, no assets, no JS. See [[self-contained-single-file-html]].
- `Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/app/` — server-side rendering over `node:http` with
  `"dependencies": {}`.

## Why: `file://` is a real constraint that bites

This is not aesthetic. `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` learned it the hard way:

> "It used to be loaded through the Babel CDN with `type=\"text/babel\"`, so opening it directly
> (`file://`) left a **blank page** — the browser blocks Babel from fetching the local `.jsx`, and
> there was no internet fallback."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/lab5_GraphTheory/README.md, 2026-07-10

The fix was to vendor React's production UMD build and commit the precompiled JSX — 2,692 inserted
lines in one commit. See [[vendor-react-over-babel-cdn]].

## The tension worth recording

`Farley` demonstrates that "offline-first" can be a value the documentation *strengthens* while the
code stays the same. The 2026-07-24 README rewrite demoted its cloud vision path from "the one
owner-chosen exception I switched on" to "ships off by default" — making the claim less accurate, not
more, since map tiles and a car-spec lookup are unconditional outbound requests. The value is real —
`classifyScreen` genuinely falls back to on-device heuristics with no API key — but the headline
overstates it. Covered on [[on-device-first-inference]] and [[opt-in-cloud-fallback]].

## Where it is contradicted

`Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories`' Q-HYDRO app sits beside two offline apps and loads Leaflet, map
tiles and fonts from CDNs, saying so plainly. `Optimization Methods` does the same for its route
explorer. Neither hides it; both are documented as graceful-degradation cases. The pattern is a strong
default, not a rule — as with [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]].
